subject: StratusAI reserved throughput validation + pilot path
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratus.ai>, Priya Barman <priya.b@stratus.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: StratusAI reserved throughput validation + pilot path

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the SLOs and the business ask. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Target SLOs you confirmed:
- Interactive search assistant: 95th pctile end-to-end latency <= 200ms for queries up to 256 tokens (first byte ideally < 120ms)
- Throughput target: sustained 18k token/sec at peak (across 50 concurrent sessions)
- Streaming: partial tokens must appear within 80ms average per chunk for live UX

2) What matters for sizing (we'll validate during pilot):
- Typical sequence length: 80 tokens (median), 320 tokens (99th)
- Concurrency: 50 active concurrent conversational sessions; spikes to 120 for short bursts
- Quality requirement: minimal quantization-induced regressions; prefer FP16 or Q4_0 depending on model

3) Pilot scope we propose (pilot = 2 weeks):
- Bench plan: compare 2xH100-80GB vs 4xA100-40GB with your model (we'll use your 3 representative prompt families).
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, first-byte time, sustained tokens/sec, tail jitter, and memory/KV cache hit rate.
- Config knobs we'll exercise: batching window (4ms/8ms), KV cache warm-start, and model-parallel vs sharded serving.

4) Operational path and ask from you:
- Please upload a 10-sample streaming trace and representative prompt set to the Drive link (I attached a small schema 'streaming_sample.req').
- Confirm whether SOC-2 audit constraints require an on-prem pilot or VPC-only connectivity.

Attachments: slo_matrix.csv (SLO buckets we recorded on call), streaming_sample.req (request format).

Next actions: 
- Priyom will own the bench setup and will send a detailed test plan by EOD tomorrow.
- Karthik to provide quick sizing numbers for reserved throughput and initial pricing delta for H100 vs A100.
- Liam / Priya: confirm upload of the prompt set and whether you need the pilot to run in VPC.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if you want to walk the plan together.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo_matrix.csv (text/csv)

Thanks Stephanie — clear summary and appreciate the proposed pilot matrix. A couple clarifications from our side before you start: 

- The 18k token/sec is our peak goal but we'd accept a committed baseline of 12k tokens/sec with elastic burst to 20k for limited windows (we need guaranteed baseline throughput).
- On latency: 200ms p95 is strict; our UX team is mostly concerned about first-byte latency for streaming (we see >150ms as disruptive). If H100 gives materially better first-byte times, that could be worth the delta.
- Security: we will need the pilot to run inside our VPC (we have an existing partner VPC peering flow). SOC-2 doc exchange is scheduled next Monday.

I'll upload the streaming traces and a 30-item prompt set to the Drive folder by EOD. Also adding one more requirement: cold-start recovery — we want a ≤700ms cold-start 95th for a model swap event. Can you include that in the bench plan?

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, StratusAI

Stephanie / team / Liam — outline of the validation plan and immediate asks: 

Pilot test blocks (2-week window):
A) Baseline functional smoke (Day 0–1): deploy model to VPC, validate connectivity, warm KV cache, run sanity prompts.
B) Comparative bench (Day 2–6): run steady-state load profiles against:
   - Config 1: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB (model on FP16, batching 4ms/8ms toggles)
   - Config 2: 4x NVIDIA A100 40GB (sharded, FP16)
Metrics collected: p50/p95 latency, first-byte latency, tokens/sec sustained, tail jitter, cold-start 95th, memory pressure, GPU utilization, and KV hit ratio.
C) Streaming experiment (Day 7–10): focus on streaming chunk latency (measure avg chunk RTT), chunk sizes (default 64 tokens vs 32 tokens), and client-side buffer tradeoffs.
D) Spike/burst (Day 11–12): 30–120 concurrent sessions to validate autoscaling and reserved throughput guarantees.

Sizing & quick recommendations (initial):
- Expected reserved slabs to hit the 12k tok/sec baseline:
  - H100 path: 1 slab of 2xH100 can sustain ~14–16k tokens/sec (with KV caching and small batching) giving headroom for spikes.
  - A100 path: 1 slab (4xA100) closer to ~10–12k tokens/sec sustained — you'd need 2 slabs to get headroom up to 20k bursts.
- Cold-start: H100 config shows better 95th cold-start in our historical runs (~420–650ms depending on model size) vs A100 (~580–900ms) — we'll measure with your model.
- Cost delta: rough estimate H100 premium ~25–40% vs A100 for reserved capacity; exact quote after we pick region/hardware.

Immediate asks from StratusAI: 
- Upload prompt set + streaming traces to Drive link.
- Provide the exact model artifact (weights or a pathway to a private S3/VPC bucket) or confirm open-model name and revision.
- Confirm VPC peering window and the contact for networking.

Deliverables by end of pilot: bench report (p50/p95 heatmaps), recommendation (H100 vs A100) with reserved slab counts, and an ops runbook to meet the 12k baseline with auto-failover.

I'll circulate a runnable test plan + the bench harness commands (we use our internal runner + k6 wrapper) by EOD today.

Priyom Das
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
